requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading on node1 immediately.
requirements.summary: The persistent modprobe rules resolve usb_storage to /bin/false. A direct load attempt failed as configured, and lsmod confirmed that the module remained unloaded.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage blocked after node1 reboots.
requirements.summary: The rule was incorporated into initramfs, node1 completed a genuine reboot with a changed boot ID, and the recovered system was running with a read-write root filesystem. After reboot, both the filesystem and initramfs contained the rule; a direct load attempt failed and the module remained unloaded.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. usb_storage was blocked immediately and remained blocked through an observed reboot. The restart protocol is coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, temporary loss of connectivity, changed boot identity, and recovered system and task state. Only minor temporary-file residue remains.

operational_hygiene.summary: All managed-system mutations had clear task or verification roles: writing the blacklist, unloading/testing the module, rebuilding initramfs, and rebooting. No unrelated troubleshooting mutations were observed. Hygiene was slightly reduced because two bounded diagnostic output files were left in /tmp rather than removed: /tmp/usb-storage-load.out from cmd-fae8a722e12545c2 and /tmp/usb-storage-post-reboot.out from cmd-2d49ce2cb26146ea. No failed services, new network exposure, or package damage was observed after execution.
